prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. TOBT=Target Off Block Time: issued only if capacity/ground path allow; frozen at horizon unless exception recorded; revised only on turnaround-actor confirmation. Modes: Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State (Business Rules Registry may tighten escalation thresholds near departure, still suppress low-impact issues), Contingency Fallback State (exception summaries via Contingency Operations Console, same role visibility). Elements: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone; Flight Intent Message vs Airport Capacity Plan; AAR=Airport Acceptance Rate); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM); Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time; Ground Delay Program; Pushback Window Token); Departure Metering Service (Emberline; TOBT protecting CTT; CTT to TSM; exception status only after Business Rules Registry materiality; includes remote stand constraints in TOBT achievability); North/South Runway Meters; Surface Surveillance Adapter; East/West Apron Sensors; Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove; Common Situation Display; Collaborative Decision Log prompts); Tower Sequence Manager (TSM, Ironleaf; SHALL NOT advance aircraft unless remote stand release time supports taxi plan); Gate Conflict Detector (Gate Reopening Memo); Airline Interface Adapter (Late Baggage Tag List to Ground Handling Dispatcher); Handling Resource Planner (exception severity; produces Remote Stand Shuttle Count periodically); Alert Distribution Hub (Lantern; MUST meet surface advisory latency); Ramp Movement Board (Skylark; Fuel Truck Hold Advice; remote stand occupancy, towing, bus readiness; MUST refresh apron layer within 5 s); Audit Event Ledger (MUST record adjustments, actors, overrides, exception lifecycle; with Identity Access Service); Sector Load Monitor (Departure Fix Load Sheet); Performance Analytics Warehouse (tunes severity thresholds vs off-block actuals); Time Synchronization Service; Arrival Regulation Console (Nightjar); Integrated Tactical Management Position; Weather Ingest Gateway (Orchard); Digital Briefing Room. Remote stands: airside resource with landside dependency; shuttle = finite resource. Actors: Airport Duty Manager (Medical Diversion Notice; publishes remote stand posture in Portal before first arrival bank), Ramp Control Lead (confirms route, transfer path, contingency per stand), Airline Operations Coordinator, Ground Handling Dispatcher (bus vs apron corridor conflicts), Tower Supervisor, Airspace Sector Planner

New part:
S554: If a bus shortage or terminal loading delay is detected, the Airline Operations Coordinator may request revision of the Target Off Block Time before the delay propagates to runway demand.
S555: The Regional Flow Manager considers repeated remote stand transfer delays as an input to tactical capacity assessment during peak arrival and departure banks.
S556: Ramp Control Lead uses the Towbar Shortage Report to determine whether remote stand aircraft can be repositioned without creating secondary apron congestion.
S557: The Capacity Assessment Module reflects persistent remote stand service limits as a reduction in practical gate throughput rather than only as a ramp movement issue.
S558: The Gate Conflict Detector identifies cases where an aircraft assigned to a contact gate would cause less overall delay than a nominally available remote stand with inadequate passenger transfer capacity.
S559: When remote stand use increases, the Airport CDM Portal records the operational reason, affected flights, expected passenger transfer duration, and responsible control position.
S560: The Common Situation Display presents remote stand status in time order so that airline, ramp, tower, and airport roles share the same expectation for aircraft readiness.
S561: Landside service limits are linked to airside timing through estimated boarding completion, bus return availability, crew access, and terminal processing constraints.
S562: A remote stand departure is not considered ready for push or tow until passengers, bags, crew, and required ground services are aligned with the planned aircraft movement.
S563: During Adverse Weather Mode, the Airport Duty Manager may reduce planned remote stand use because bus loading, walking routes, and accessible transfer times become less predictable.
S564: During Recovery Phase, remote stands may be used to absorb late arrivals while preserving contact gates for flights with tight turnarounds or high connection sensitivity.
S565: The Performance Analytics Warehouse retains remote stand timing measures so that planners can compare scheduled assumptions with actual passenger transfer and apron release performance.
S566: This section extends the remote stand performance concept by describing how border, customs, and apron sensing inputs become constraints in the daily operating plan.
S567: Border release status is represented as a readiness attribute on each affected flight record in the Regional Flow Platform, separate from aircraft readiness and airline commercial readiness.
S568: The Airport Duty Manager produces the Customs Hold Release Note when border processing confirms that a held arrival may proceed to normal turnaround handling.
S569: Customs hold indicators are represented as operational constraints that prevent premature stand release, passenger transfer assumptions, or departure readiness claims.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
